::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
SK Hynix's Chongqing back-end (2013 agreement, mass production 2014, phase-2 2019, ~$1.2B cumulative) — the assembly/test counterpart to its Wuxi DRAM and Dalian NAND fabs, and the reason the Korean memory maker's China exposure is not only about wafer fabs.
:::

**Chinese name:** 爱思开海力士半导体（重庆）有限公司 (Àisīkāi Hǎilìshì Bàndǎotǐ (Chóngqìng))

## What does this facility make?

Packaging and test of NAND flash modules/SSD components.

## Why does it matter?

As of August 2026 SK Hynix is reportedly weighing options incl. selling a stake (~$3B valuation, possible Chinese fund buyers) while keeping the site running — the first major case of a Korean memory back-end in China facing a divest-or-double-down decision under tool-control pressure.

## Project Timeline

- **Jul 2013** — Site founded and breaks ground (2013-05 agreement)
- **Sep 2014** — Mass production begins (~$250-300M phase 1)
- **Sep 2019** — Phase-2 completed; cumulative investment ~$1.2B
- **Aug 2026** — Stake-sale options reported (~$3B valuation); no decision confirmed
